# M20-S0: cgo in loGo/s packages. A package whose c_bridge.lgo imports "C"
# and holds Go syntax only builds beside other .lgo files that use ? and
# unions. The cgo layout is the upstream one: cmd/cgo names its outputs
# from the source file and the compiler takes them with the .lgo files.
# Pointers C returns are platform pointers: a NULL stored into a declared
# non-nil location panics with the checked-store message instead of
# reaching loGo/s code as a non-nil value. loGo/s syntax in a file that
# imports "C" fails with the pinned rule text; a plain Go syntax error in
# the same file and loGo/s syntax in a .go cgo file keep the parser text.
[!cgo] skip 'cgo is not available'

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# Default CC: a host compiler setting must not drive the build.
env CC=

# The bridge and the other .lgo files build and run as one package.
logos build -x -o $WORK/ok.bin ./ok
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo\.cgo1\.go'
stderr '_cgo_gotypes\.go'
exec $WORK/ok.bin
stdout '^sum: 42$'
stdout '^bad: true$'
stdout '^num:42$'
stdout '^str:none$'
stdout '^find: id:7$'
stdout '^stored: id:7$'
stdout '^next: 7$'
stdout '^item: 0$'

# A NULL from C stored into a non-nil location panics; neither a return
# nor a declared variable lets it reach loGo/s code unchecked.
# The panic names the .lgo source and its line, not the generated file.
stdout '^find-missing: logos: nil from Go value stored into non-nil \*main\._Ctype_struct_item at c_bridge\.lgo:39$'
stdout '^stored-missing: logos: nil from Go value stored into non-nil \*main\._Ctype_struct_item at c_bridge\.lgo:44$'

# loGo/s syntax in a file that imports "C" fails with the pinned text at
# the first loGo/s token. The parser errors that follow stay unprinted.
! logos build -o $WORK/badtry.bin ./badtry
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:13:22: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'
! stderr 'illegal character'
! stderr 'expected'

! logos build -o $WORK/badlambda.bin ./badlambda
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:11: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badinterp.bin ./badinterp
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:9: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badspread.bin ./badspread
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:10:14: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/baddot.bin ./baddot
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:11:3: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

# The plain-token loGo/s families fail the same way: errdefer, yield,
# scope defer, go group and go child blocks, const if/for/switch, and
# tuples. Each pin names the first loGo/s spelling in the file.
! logos build -o $WORK/baderrdefer.bin ./baderrdefer
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badyield.bin ./badyield
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badscopedefer.bin ./badscopedefer
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badgroup.bin ./badgroup
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badgochild.bin ./badgochild
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badconstif.bin ./badconstif
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badconstfor.bin ./badconstfor
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:10:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badconstswitch.bin ./badconstswitch
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:2: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

! logos build -o $WORK/badtuple.bin ./badtuple
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:9:20: \[correctness::cgo_file_logos_syntax\] files that import "C" must use Go syntax only$'

# A bridge-only package (no other .lgo files) still checks a NULL from C
# stored into a declared non-nil location.
logos build -o $WORK/bridge.bin ./okbridge
! exec $WORK/bridge.bin
stderr 'logos: nil from Go value stored into non-nil \*main\._Ctype_int at c_bridge\.lgo:10$'

# Characters of loGo/s syntax inside comments and strings are Go syntax,
# and an ordinary Go syntax error is not loGo/s syntax: the parser text
# stays and the loGo/s rule never fires.
! logos build -o $WORK/goerr.bin ./goerr
stderr 'c_bridge\.lgo:8:[0-9]+: expected'
! stderr 'cgo_file_logos_syntax'

# A .go cgo file is not a loGo/s input: plain go keeps the parser text.
cd gomod
! go build ./...
stderr 'illegal character U\+003F'
! stderr 'cgo_file_logos_syntax'
cd ..

-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.27

-- logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "allow"

-- ok/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
#include <stddef.h>

struct item {
	int id;
	struct item *next;
};

static struct item the_item = {7, 0};

static int c_add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }

static struct item *c_find(int id) {
	if (id == 7) {
		return &the_item;
	}
	return NULL;
}

static struct item *c_next(struct item *n) {
	if (n->next != 0) {
		return n->next;
	}
	return n;
}
*/
import "C"

// Add calls C and returns a Go int.
func Add(a, b int) int {
	return int(C.c_add(C.int(a), C.int(b)))
}

// Find returns the item with the given id. C returns NULL for a missing
// id, and the result is a pointer in a non-nil result.
func Find(id int) *C.struct_item {
	return C.c_find(C.int(id))
}

// Stored keeps the C result in a declared non-nil variable and reads it.
func Stored(id int) int {
	var it *C.struct_item = C.c_find(C.int(id))
	return int(it.id)
}

// ID reads the id of an item.
func ID(it *C.struct_item) int {
	return int(it.id)
}

// Next returns the item after n, or n itself at the tail.
func Next(n *C.struct_item) *C.struct_item {
	return C.c_next(n)
}

// ZeroItem declares a C item value; pointer fields of C structs stay
// nilable under Go semantics.
func ZeroItem() C.struct_item {
	var n C.struct_item
	return n
}

-- ok/app.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
)

type Num struct {
	N int
}

type Str struct {
	S string
}

// Value is a closed union of Num and Str.
type Value interface {
	Num | Str
	Describe() string
}

func (n Num) Describe() string {
	return "num:" + strconv.Itoa(n.N)
}

func (s Str) Describe() string {
	return "str:" + s.S
}

func pick(n int) Value {
	if n > 0 {
		return Num{N: n}
	}
	return Str{S: "none"}
}

// total adds two numbers through the C bridge; ? returns the parse error.
func total(a, b string) (int, error) {
	x := strconv.Atoi(a)?
	y := strconv.Atoi(b)?
	return Add(x, y), nil
}

func tryFind(id int) (msg string) {
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			msg = fmt.Sprint(r)
		}
	}()
	return "id:" + strconv.Itoa(ID(Find(id)))
}

func tryStored(id int) (msg string) {
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			msg = fmt.Sprint(r)
		}
	}()
	return "id:" + strconv.Itoa(Stored(id))
}

func main() {
	sum, err := total("40", "2")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("error:", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Println("sum:", sum)
	_, err = total("x", "2")
	fmt.Println("bad:", err != nil)
	fmt.Println(pick(sum).Describe())
	fmt.Println(pick(0).Describe())
	fmt.Println("find:", tryFind(7))
	fmt.Println("stored:", tryStored(7))
	fmt.Println("find-missing:", tryFind(9))
	fmt.Println("stored-missing:", tryStored(9))
	fmt.Println("next:", int(Next(Find(7)).id))
	fmt.Println("item:", int(ZeroItem().id))
}

-- badtry/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

import "strconv"

// parse uses ?, which a file that imports "C" cannot.
func parse(s string) (int, error) {
	// A comment with ? and $"x" is fine.
	n := strconv.Atoi(s)?
	return n + int(C.c_one()), nil
}

func main() {}

-- badlambda/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

func main() {
	inc := x => x + int(C.c_one())
	_ = inc
}

-- badinterp/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

func main() {
	msg := $"one={C.c_one()}"
	_ = msg
}

-- badspread/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

func main() {
	xs := []int{int(C.c_one())}
	ys := []int{..xs}
	_ = ys
}

-- baddot/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

func main() {
	n := int(C.c_one())
	s := fmt.Sprint(n)
		.trim()
	_ = s
}

	_ = 1
}

-- badconstif/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

func main() {
	const if true {
		_ = C.c_one()
	}
}

*/

func main() {
	xs := []int{int(C.c_one())}
	const for x := range xs {
	}
}

	}

-- okbridge/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
#include <stddef.h>
static int *c_null(void) { return 0; }
*/
import "C"

func main() {
	var p *C.int = C.c_null()
	println(int(*p))
}

-- goerr/c_bridge.lgo --
package main

/*
int c_one(void) { return 1; }
*/
import "C"

func broken( {
	_ = C.c_one()
	_ = "what? $\"x\" a => b"
}

	n := int(C.c_one())?
	_ = n
